summary: Analysis of the 14-day Nightscout telemetry demonstrates exceptionally stable glycemic control with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%), and 0.0% Time Below Range. Basal rates, CR, ISF, and DIA settings align well with physiological needs, supported effectively by background SMB/UAM automation.

analysis_steps.findings: Data quality and completeness are excellent across the 14-day period with 100% CGM coverage, zero gaps, and complete treatment records.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 CGM entries collected at a consistent 15-minute cadence with zero gaps greater than 15 minutes; 28 meal boluses and an authoritative active AAPS profile present.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic patterns reflect high safety with minimal variability and no recorded clinical hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%, 99.7% TIR, 0.3% TAR (>180 mg/dL), and 0.0% TBR (<70 mg/dL). Minimum reading was 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and fasting basal segments maintain flat, target-level glucose without needing manual or loop corrections.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local mean glucose (00:00-06:00) remains between 102 and 112 mg/dL, matching profile target bands (95-110 mg/dL overnight, 90-105 mg/dL morning).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unannounced daytime fasting windows are limited due to regular meal timing.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios, ISF values, and 5.5-hour DIA accurately match meal absorption and decay profiles.
analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial glucose peaks average 145.6 mg/dL at breakfast and 136.5 mg/dL at brunch, returning smoothly to target baseline within 3 to 4 hours post-meal with no late hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM micro-bolusing operate within safe parameters, smoothing postprandial curves without over-delivering insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB enabled, UAM enabled, SMB interval 3 min, max SMB basal minutes 45 min, max UAM SMB basal minutes 30 min. Zero TBR confirms no insulin stacking from micro-boluses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific SMB activation boolean flags in raw settings are unpopulated (null) in the export.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety caps (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom without masking profile defects.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal is ~2.3x peak scheduled basal (1.05 U/h). Stable fasting glucose indicates automation is modulating around an accurate baseline rather than compensating for incorrect profile parameters.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens explicit boolean enable flags are null in the export.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal bolus strategies (20 min prebolus for weekday breakfast, 10 min prebolus for weekend brunch) successfully limit postprandial spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 meal boluses analyzed. Weekday breakfast (42g) glucose rises by +33 to +57 mg/dL at 120 min before returning to baseline at 240-360 min.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs configuration (20g over 120m for high-fat weekend brunch) prevents late postprandial hyperglycemia and insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch (68g total) peaks at 188 mg/dL at 120 min and returns to ~111 mg/dL by 240-360 min without secondary rises or drops.

analysis_steps.findings: All profile and automation settings are operating harmoniously. No parameter modifications are required; maintenance and verification are recommended.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consistent 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, stable fasting trends, and predictable postprandial response across 14 days.

strengths: Outstanding Time in Range (99.7%) with zero time spent below 70 mg/dL across 14 days.
Exceptionally low glycemic variability (CV of 12.9% and SD of 15.1 mg/dL).
Accurate basal rates keeping overnight glucose perfectly flat in the 100-110 mg/dL range.
Effective meal strategy using preboluses and e-carbs to keep postprandial peaks under control.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Profile Parameters
recommendations.description: All basal rates, carb ratios, ISF segments, targets, and DIA settings are currently optimal. No changes are indicated by the 14-day telemetry.

recommendations.title: Verify Unpopulated AAPS Settings in Preference UI
recommendations.description: Certain raw AAPS activation parameters (e.g. smb_always_enabled, autosens_enabled) are returned as null in export metadata. Confirm that UI options reflect your intended setup.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA parameters unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: With 99.7% Time in Range, 0.0% Hypoglycemia, and stable overnight glucose, current profile settings are fully optimized.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate after 30 days or if a routine change in lifestyle or meal habits occurs.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Administer a 20-minute prebolus with 100% immediate bolus for fast-carb meals (or 60-70% immediate if using e-carbs for slower absorption), allowing background AAPS SMB/UAM to manage residual postprandial variations.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: This combined approach yields 99.7% TIR and eliminates postprandial spikes without causing early or late hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal composition for novel high-fat or late evening meals to assess if e-carbs or split timing can further optimize postprandial stability.

exceptions.suggestion: Use a 10-minute prebolus with 60% immediate bolus and 20g declared as e-carbs over 120 minutes (15-minute offset).
exceptions.rationale: Matches slower gastric emptying of higher-fat meals, flattening the 120-minute peak without trailing hypoglycemia.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain a 20-minute prebolus with 100% immediate bolus and no e-carbs.
exceptions.rationale: Blunts rapid carbohydrate absorption, keeping 2-hour postprandial glucose within safe limits.

implementation_steps: Review current analysis results with your clinical care team.
Retain all active AAPS basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA profile parameters without alteration.
Check AAPS preference UI to confirm that unpopulated export fields (such as SMB activation triggers) match desired operational settings.
Continue logging meal types and using preboluses and e-carbs according to declared strategies.
education: A 5.5-hour Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) helps automated systems accurately model residual insulin on board (IOB) and prevents insulin stacking.
E-carbs allow automated systems to extend simulated carbohydrate absorption (COB) over time, matching high-fat or high-protein meals better than a large single bolus.
Stable overnight glucose in the absence of food or manual corrections is the primary indicator of accurate basal rates.
safety_notes: This output is decision-support content for review only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always independently verify proposed settings and consult your healthcare provider before changing insulin therapy parameters.
Make parameter changes one at a time and monitor glucose closely following any adjustment.
